geometry_edits.rationale: Align the public threshold notch to the verified access edge so the ground response reads toward the street frontage rather than away from it.
Widen the access carve slightly to make the entry seam and public opening more legible in plan and perspective.
Deepen the vertical extent of the carve so the street threshold becomes a more usable public void rather than a shallow indentation.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing with a readable dominant bent bar and a secondary threshold carve/notch system. Across the four views it holds together reasonably well and does not visibly self-collide, so repair integrity is solid. The main weakness is that the public response to the verified access edge is only moderately legible: there is a notch/cantilever language, but the access-facing ground condition still reads more as a compact object than a clearly activated street threshold or court. The silhouette is acceptable as a continuous mass, though the stepped/eroded upper edge is somewhat generic rather than strongly program-serving. For neighborhood living, the form can plausibly support the brief because it maintains a dominant occupied volume, an upper hierarchy, and some void logic; however, section/program fit would improve with a clearer carved public zone or access-aligned opening. The references collectively support courtyard/bridge/terrace strategies and a compact community-building language.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise composed mass with a clear central void and an upper connector/bridge can support neighborhood-program publicness.
